requirements.title: ASSOCIATE execution evaluates selectors before executing the block
requirements.source: 11.1.3.2 p1 first sentence; J3/24-007 PDF p204.
requirements.definition: Executing an ASSOCIATE construct evaluates every expression within every selector that is a variable designator and evaluates every other selector, followed by execution of the block. This establishes selector values or variable associations before block execution; it does not prescribe expression evaluation order among selectors or authorize side-effect/count oracles.

pending.block-executes-after-selector-evaluation: PENDING positive-control source shape where the block assigns through an associate name only after selector association is established, with direct final value checks.

requirements.oracle:
Use side-effect-free selector expressions and direct values. Do not infer order among multiple selector evaluations or count evaluations.

S11.1.3.2-001 ASSOCIATE selector-evaluation runtime fixtures: two complete run/effect/f2023 programs observe selector evaluation before ASSOCIATE block execution without side-effect or call-count oracles. The expression-selector case evaluates seed+17 while seed is 23, then changes seed to -900 inside the block and reads the associate name as literal 40; a rule that re-evaluated after the block assignment would produce -883. The variable-designator case uses a(idx) with idx=2, changes idx to 4 inside the block, assigns through cell, and checks that a(2) becomes 77 while a(4) remains 44; a deferred-subscript rule would update the wrong element. The selector expressions are ordinary integer expressions and the observations are final scalar values plus exact completion stdout.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future ASSOCIATE fixtures must use non-vacuous selectors and sentinels: lower bounds must differ where bounds are asserted, character length must be checked with LEN rather than inferred from padded comparison, outer homonyms must start with values different from any inner assignment, and assignment through an associate name is credited only after the selector is established definable. No plan may count selector evaluations, depend on function side effects, assume a real or complex kind exists, or use compiler agreement as an oracle.

S11.1.3.2-001 ASSOCIATE selector-evaluation fixture boundaries: only expression-selector-value-before-block and variable-designator-subexpressions-before-block are represented. block-executes-after-selector-evaluation remains pending because this packet does not try to separate ordinary block execution from the stronger association/assignment effects covered elsewhere. The programs do not observe evaluation order among multiple selectors, function side effects, call counts, undefined values, diagnostics, addresses or temporary storage.

requirements.title: During the ASSOCIATE block each associate name identifies an entity associated with its selector
requirements.source: 11.1.3.2 p1 second sentence; J3/24-007 PDF p204.
requirements.definition: During execution of the ASSOCIATE block, each associate name identifies an entity associated with the corresponding selector. The lifetime/scope of that construct entity and the general association relation are Clause 19 dependencies.
requirements.oracle:
Association is observable through values and assignments only when selector definability is established. Scope diagnostics are not attributed to this descriptive sentence alone.

S11.1.3.2-002 ASSOCIATE association runtime fixtures: three complete run/effect/f2023 programs observe the associate name identifying the associated entity during the block. The expression-read case binds expr_value to left*10+right with left=12 and right=5, changes both operands in the block, and requires expr_value to remain 125. The variable-selector case binds alias to target, assigns alias=271 inside the block, and observes target changed from 314 to 271. The scope case preloads an outer integer named item with sentinel 707, binds the associate name item to target, writes only 303 through the associate name, and after END ASSOCIATE requires outer item still 707 and target 303. Thus the outer sentinel is distinct from every value written inside the construct.

requirements.title: ASSOCIATE associating entities assume selector declared type, type parameters, and polymorphic status
requirements.source: 11.1.3.2 p1 final sentences; J3/24-007 PDF p204.
requirements.definition: The associating entity assumes the declared type and type parameters of the selector. If and only if the selector is polymorphic, the associating entity is polymorphic. Dynamic type and additional attributes are owned by 11.1.3.3.

pending.kind-type-parameter-source: PENDING source-control plan using a selector with an explicitly declared kind chosen through available-kind logic, without assuming a particular real or complex kind exists.
pending.polymorphic-selector-control: PENDING source-control plan with a polymorphic selector and associate name in a context requiring polymorphism, after polymorphic entities and SELECT TYPE dependencies are registered.
pending.nonpolymorphic-selector-control: PENDING source-control plan showing a nonpolymorphic selector does not make the associating entity polymorphic; any negative must be filed under the rule requiring polymorphism.

requirements.oracle:
LEN/KIND or source admissibility may observe type parameters only when the expected value is required by declarations in the same test. Do not assume processor-dependent kind availability.

S11.1.3.2-003 ASSOCIATE type-parameter runtime fixture: one complete run/effect/f2023 program observes a required character type parameter directly with LEN. The selector is the substring parent(3:8) of a CHARACTER(LEN=9) variable, so the selector's length type parameter is 6 by the substring endpoints and the associating entity must assume that value. The program checks LEN(slice)==6 explicitly; no blank-padded character comparison is used as a length oracle. A rule copying the parent length 9, using default length 1, or otherwise not assuming the selector type parameter would fail.

review_rationale: Renewal of the content-bound source review for 11.1.3.2 after a fixture packet bound facets into this catalogue. Adding a facet binding changes catalogue content and therefore stales the recorded source review by design; this renewal records that the staleness is attributable solely to the binding. The SOURCE ACCOUNTING IS UNCHANGED by the fixture packets: no base or fine unit was added, removed or redispositioned, no requirement was added or deleted, no requirement identifier was renumbered or reused, and the section's unit hashes against the pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...) are exactly those verified by the original independent source review recorded in the corresponding doc/source_audits receipt. What changed is that facets which were previously pending are now bound to executable fixtures, each of which was independently reviewed as a fixture in its own right, with non-vacuity established by mutation rather than inspection and with the frozen LFortran and the gfortran f2023 qualifying reference both reproduced by the integrator before any adjudication was recorded. This renewal therefore carries forward the original source review's findings unchanged and adds no new source claim. It is not fixture approval, which is recorded separately per case in tests/reviews.json, and it confers no additional execution or coverage credit beyond what those per-case adjudications already state. All facets not bound by a fixture packet remain pending exactly as the original source review left them.
